text:
caroline: Heads-up — customer Acme reported intermittent 504s on hosted text-gen API starting ~09:15 UTC. They see long tail latencies (p99 > 12s) and some requests failing with gateway timeouts. Repro steps attached.
ryan: Thanks. Any request IDs or sample traces from the gateway? Could be continuous-batcher backlog + queue-depth hitting the soft limit.
maria: Got two request IDs from customer: rQ-9a7f and rQ-9a8c. Customer says failures happen on long-context requests (~1k tokens) and batch size ~8.
sam: infra alert just fired: `ingress.batcher.queue_depth >= 95%` across hostpool-3 for the last 10m. infra-bot posted alert: "hosted: ingress batcher queue approaching capacity (95%)."
infra-bot: ALERT hostpool-3 ingress queue high (95%) | continuous-batcher backlog rising | p95 enqueue latency 400ms -> 2.4s
caroline: Customer repro (short curl):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-8k","input":"<~1k tokens>","max_tokens":1024}'
```

They got back a 504 and this snippet in response body: { "error": "gateway timeout", "request_id": "rQ-9a7f" }.
ryan: Looks like the continuous batching pipeline is accumulating large KV cache warmups and long seqs are creating imbalanced batch composition. That increases per-batch latency and fills the request queue. Need traces for batcher dequeue times and per-batch token counts.
maria: I pulled traces for rQ-9a7f: `enqueue_time: 83ms, queue_wait: 11.6s, batch_dispatch_delay: 11.5s, model_infer: 1.1s` — so the delay is in queueing, not model inference.
sam: We're also seeing elevated cold-KV hits on that pool: kv_cache_miss_rate ~ 27% (baseline 3%). Cold starts + long contexts are compounding.
support-engineer: I've already replied to customer acknowledging and asked for any recent spike in request volume or unusual prompt patterns. Also asked for exact timestamps. They responded that it started after a step-change in usage they rolled out at 09:00 UTC.
caroline: Immediate mitigations we can try:
- route Acme to hostpool-5 (lower utilization) via an emergency routing override
- temporarily reduce batch size limit for redwood-open-8k on hostpool-3
- enable KV-cache prewarm for tenant if supported
- fallback single-request slow path for requests that exceed 800 tokens
ryan: I can do the routing override. Changing batch size limits requires a rollout but we can push a hot config to hostpool-3: `batch.size.max=4` for the model to reduce head-of-line blocking.
maria: Also recommend a short term autoscale bump for hostpool-3 GPUs (add 2 nodes) to drain backlog. I'll open an infra job to add capacity.
sam: Traces show some tenant-level burst with many long-context requests arriving in parallel. If they keep this pattern, we need a long-term limiter or adaptive batching.
support-engineer: I'll update the customer: letting them know we routed them to hostpool-5 and we're applying mitigations. Asking them to monitor and report request IDs if they still see 504s.
caroline: Follow-ups: (1) post-incident, we should add a throttling rule for >800 token single requests that routes to a slower but isolated path, (2) improve metrics to surface `enqueue_time` and `batch_hold_time` per-tenant in Console, (3) consider per-tenant KV prewarm or priority lane.
ryan: On it. I'll document the hotfix steps and post the CLI commands I used in this thread. For now, keep this thread for updates and customer replies.
maria: Capacity job submitted, ETA +6m to spin new nodes.
support-engineer: Customer confirmed routing override helped: "latencies dropped to normal range, no 504s for 12m" :thumbsup:
caroline: Great. We'll keep monitoring 30m and then close. Postmortem action items logged in our incident tracker.
